text:
The story in Buffalo this month has been the crease. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled in a rout by Tampa Bay on Nov. 12, Alex Lyon then lost three straight, and the questions got loud. Thursday, Luukkonen answered with a 6-3 win in Washington, and Tage Thompson's postgame line in the team's video said it plainly: "I loved Our Response."

Goaltending is not really the main problem, though. The Sabres have allowed only 2.5 more goals than their chances against suggest. The bigger gap is at the other end: they have scored about six fewer goals than their chances deserved, which is how a team with 49% of the expected goals ends up 9-9-4 with four overtime losses.

The bright spot is a young line. Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have outscored teams 8-4 at 5-on-5 and controlled 59% of the expected goals, the best process of any regular trio here. It comes at a good time for Quinn, whose next contract is already a topic (The Athletic asked what he might cost). The top pair, Rasmus Dahlin and Mattias Samuelsson, sits just under even on chances.

Our numbers give Buffalo a 21% chance at the playoffs in the Atlantic. Next up is a Florida and Tampa Bay back-to-back this weekend, a fair test of whether Thursday was a turn or a blip.
headline: A crease in question, a line worth keeping
